en:
A-Aniki!? What's goin' on?
I didn't know y'were comin' back.
Sorry I didn't tell you guys.

Where's Yuta, though?
He okay?
Yeah. He stayed behind in Kamurocho.
Jus' what happened up there, Aniki?

That's what I'm here to talk to you about.
Have a seat, guys.
I dunno if I follow, Aniki.

So the boss was usin' Yuta t'kill Lo
,
and... he was plannin' t'have Yuta die, too.
It kinda sounds like that's what yer sayin'.

Funny y'say that, Cap.
That's what I heard, too.
I'm only repeating what Lo told me.

Either way, where is Patriarch Hirose now?
How long has it been since you last saw him?
Y'know how often he wanders around town.
He'll probly be back soon.

According to Lo, if I attempt to expose the secret
of Onomichi, your boss will do anything to stop me.

To be blunt, he'll try to kill me,
just like with Yuta and Big Lo.

But how can y'jus' trust Lo
without any goddamn proof!?
Right, not saying I do.
Y'know 'bout me n' Matsunaga, Aniki?

Ever since we were jus' rugrats,
Patriarch Hirose's watched over us.

Our dads were gone fer good,
so he took us in, protected us.

Whatever yer thinkin' the Hirose Family's
history
 is, yer way wrong.
N' y'really think we'll believe this triad bullshit?
I ain't gonna doubt the boss that easy!

Whaddya say t'that!?
Huh, Kiryu-aniki!?

Lo's given you a tough pill to swallow.
I don't expect you to believe him.
I honestly don't want to, either.

So y'don't wanna believe,
but y'still do anyways, huh?

In that case, <font_kind=yakuza_italic>Kiryu-san</font_kind>... Yer done here.
Y'ain't our aniki anymore.

Fine, but... If he shows up to protect the
the secret of Onomichi? What then?

We ain't dumb enough t'go
behind his back on it.

It's our jobs t'shut our mouths n' listen, right?
Y'should know yakuza rules better than anyone.
Suddenly you care about yakuza protocol?
Hey. The hell'd ya just say, <font_kind=yakuza_italic>Kiryu-san</font_kind>!?

He's right. Y'think y'can jus'
come at our cap like that!?
Keep yer hands off o' him.

Outside now, Kiryu. 
It's high time we settled this fer real.

I didn't expect I'd have to fight you again, Nagumo.
I don't really want to hit you.

Don't matter what y'want.
All I know is, I ain't gonna hold back.

This time yer gonna see the real
spirit of the Hiroshima yakuza!
Now fight me like y'mean it!

Whaddya shits think yer doin'? I ain't done yet.
Get yer asses back inside!
That ain't it, Cap.
We got guests.
Main family guys.
We can finish this later, Nagumo.
Wait, what're those punks here for?

Probably more of Chairman Kurusu's thugs.
I'm pretty sure he doesn't want me here.

What, y'mean 'cause yer tryin'
t'reveal the secret o' Onomichi?

This isn't your problem, Nagumo.
Just tell them you've cut ties with me.
They'll let you guys go if you do that.
No way're we gonna be that pathetic.
Y'ready fer this, Cap?
Let's show these main family bitches what's up.

They're gonna see what it means
t'mess with the Hirose Family!

Chairman Kurusu will stop at nothing to protect
the secret of Onomichi. You see that now?

Yeah, clear as day. Even so
,
that don't mean the boss is in on it.

If you trust him, you shouldn't be
afraid to prove your conviction.

Will you be able to keep calling him your
patriarch if you never know the truth?

Are your Hirose Family bonds so weak that
you have to ignore this to keep them intact?
'Course not.

Huh? So uh, we gonna help
reveal the secret with 'im, Cap?

But... What if the boss really is out
t'get whoever tries t'go fer the secret?
I don't give a flyin' fuck about what-ifs!

That ain't how we're gonna run
this show from here on out!

Y'know, a real family is second guessin'
their patriarch at every turn!
I've gone n' made up my mind.

Let's do this. I wanna expose
the secret o' Onomichi.

But, y'best know this<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>I'm only doin'
this shit to clear the boss's name.

N' once I manage that
,
y'gonna be ready fer some real damn apologies?

Yeah. If that's how this goes down,
you have my word.

And y'can't go back on that promise...
Kiryu-aniki.

Yer back t'callin' him Aniki, huh?
D'ya ever stop changin' yer mind...?

I expect ya t'do the same, Matsunaga.
You too, Tagashira.

Well? How exactly do we go about
gettin' our hands on this secret?

Lo left this to me. It's a code that will
point to the secret's location.

But there's one problem. Not Lo or
anyone else has cracked it yet.

If we're going to solve this riddle,
we need to work as a team.
This is the image Lo gave to me.

What the shit? Y'sure this thing's
really the whole code?

Yeah. Apparently, it'll lead us
to a particular location.

Lemme see. The letters here are
J, B, R, N, M, E, O, I, and K.

And then the numbers're
7, 7, 36, 1, 7, 9, 22, 1, and 1.

The way they're organized kinda makes it
look like each letter's paired with a number.

Hold on a sec, this might be
some kinda substitution cipher.
What is that?
It's a type o' code I read about online.

Look here. The first pair gives ya J7
and the second pair leaves us with B7.

If we can decode those pairs somehow
,
it'll probly make a phrase or somethin'.

But... we're gonna need the substitution table
if we wanna solve this thing.

It's a list o' the letters
that the code's based on.
Fer example, take the 50 hiragana characters.

One way t'encode 'em as numbers would
be on a table kinda like this.

So then if you wanted t'use this table to
write out "konnichiwa"...
Damn, that's crazy.

So then... we just gotta figure out what
kinda table Lo's code is usin', right?
Yer exactly right.

Lo mentioned that solving this would require
someone who really knew Onomichi well.

To throw it out there, maybe the table is
connected to the area's history somehow.
All right, we got this!

Let's turn the whole damn town upside down.
We gotta look fer anythin' that might help us!
Cap n' Matsunaga're out searchin' the town.
I'm gonna keep lookin' online fer clues, though.

Hmmm? I ain't seen y'round here before.
Y'from outta town or somethin'?
Onomichi's a magical place, y'know.

People've been comin' from all over t'see
this picturesque port town fer centuries.

Even tons o' famous authors n' poets've
been charmed by its unique allure.

So much so that they left poems
dedicated t'the place.

Our ancestors wanted future generations t'enjoy
these poems too, so they carved 'em onto stones.

If y'ever have the chance, y'might wanna
take a gander at the poem stones they left us.
Good idea.

There're nine of 'em in total. I bet y'won't
have any trouble findin' them 'round town.
Thanks for the info.
(This looks like a poem stone.)

(The sun setting over the Onomichi coastline
really is a stunning sight to behold.)
(Jippensha Ikku... The first letter of his name is J.)

(I wonder if this is related to the code.
Maybe I should get a picture, just in case.)
(I don't like fighting on an empty stomach, either...)
(Basho... The first letter of his name is B.)

(Overlooking Onomichi at dusk, drink in hand...
That sounds incredible.)
(Rai Sanyo... The first letter of his name is R.)

(I can't help but think of flowers in bloom
surveying a blood-soaked battlefield.)
(Natsume Soseki... The first letter of his name is N.)

(Two pagodas peeking out over the mountains...
The perfect image for a hilly town like Onomichi.)
(Masaoka Shiki... The first letter of his name is M.)

(I get the sense that those islands fading in and out
of view held great sentimental value for him.)
(Emi Suiin... The first letter of his name is E.)

(It's rare to find a city bordered by ocean on one side
and mountains on the other. Onomichi is special.)
(Ogata Koan... The first letter of his name is O.)

(Countless tile-roofed temples dot the mountainside.
Onomichi must have been lively in its prime.)
(Iwaya Sazanami... The first letter of his name is I.)

(I might actually not mind being buried if it meant
being surrounded by a chorus of chirping birds.)
(Kobayashi Issa... The first letter of his name is K.)
(I've checked all nine poem stones.)

(The first letters of the author's names
come out to J, B, R, N, M, E, O, I, and K.)

(I'm on to something. The names
match up perfectly to the code.)

(I should head back to the office
and let the others know...)

Yer back, Kiryu-aniki!
Y'figure anythin' out?
Yeah. You all should hear this.

I ended up at all nine of
the poem stones around town.

As it turns out, the first letter of each author's
name matches up with the letters of the code.

I have photos of each stone to prove it to you.
Take a look, Tagashira.
N-No way! These really do match!

Maybe the substitution table fer the code
is actually carved on the poem stones!

Kiryu-aniki!
Y'done real good!

If yer right, don't that mean we can
solve the code?
Yup. Let's get crackin'!

J7 would be the seventh kanji of
Jippensha Ikku's poem: "sea."

B7 is the seventh kanji of
Basho's poem: "army."
Lemme just figure out the rest.

Sea, army, water, soldier, mountain
name, road, big, grave.

Those kanji combine t'make...
"Naval soldier Yamano Dodai's grave."

Wait, y'mean the big grave up in
the cemetery behind the highway?

Yer right!
That's gotta be the place!

That'll do, then. Kiryu-aniki!
Let's get
 on over t'the cemetery!

Here we are.
Says right here... Yamano Dodai.
So the secret is in this grave.

Kiryu-aniki, I'm gonna pry it open.
I might need yer help, though.
We jus' gotta take a little peek.
Nothin' wrong with that, right?
Here goes nothin'...
Find anything?
Hm? Somethin's back here!
Kiryu-aniki, maybe y'oughta do the honors.
What is this?

Is that one o' the blueprints fer
the old Iwami shipyard?

If I'm rememberin' right, that's where
they made ships up 'til the war started.

It's pretty damn old now, though. I think
the whole place is closed off.
So Lo's code points to the shipyard.

There's no doubt. That's where
the secret of Onomichi is hidden.

We can probly use the boat Ino lent us
when we were chasin' Joon-gi Han.
That'd be perfect fer gettin' to the shipyard.

Cap. I bet there're gonna be tons o' main family
guys on our way down t'the dock.
Y'mind if I knock a few heads on the way?

Be my guest.
We don't gotta hold back anymore.
C'mon, Aniki. Let's head over t'Ino's boat.
Heeey! Heard y'need a boat!
Hurry up n' get on!

All right, Aniki.
Y'ready fer this?
Yeah. Let's do it.

Okay, Aniki.
Jus' lemme know when y'are.
Y'finally good t'go, Aniki?

Aniki. This Iwami shipyard place...
It's real freakin' big.

If that code don't take us right t'the secret
,
we're gonna be up shit creek.

It's our only clue, though. If we don't go,
we won't find anything for sure.

Y'can't deny that the code was
pointin' straight t'the shipyard.

I've actually wandered around the place
a bit myself, so I know the lay o' the land.
I can point ya in the right direction.
Great, thanks.

Anyways, whaddya think we're gonna dig up?
I wonder what this secret o' Onomichi really is.
I'm not sure. Not even Lo knew the truth...

Looks like they knew we'd come, Aniki.
These guys're main family boys fer sure.

Let's stick together, guys.
Stay close to me.
It's time.

Hell yeah, we did it! Serves y'bitches right!
Yer no match fer us, y'goddamn pussies!

No way this is over, though.
I'm sure there'll be more of 'em.
As fer the code, it was pointin' this way.
C'mon. Follow me, y'guys.
Let's try usin' this elevator.

We still got a long way t'go before we reach
where the code was pointin'. Let's hurry.
They jus' don't know when t'quit.

No lettin' up now. Make 'em
regret even raisin' their fists!
Aniki. We gotta keep movin'.

Wait, the hell's goin' on here?
Ain't this jus' a dead end?
Shit! They must've blocked the path!

They're gonna catch us at this rate!
What do we do?
I'll handle it.

Kiryu-aniki!
You're crazy!
Sonuvabitch... More of 'em.
Guys, we gotta keep goin'!

Y'guys can go on without me fer now.
I'll hold 'em back long as I can.

No fussin' now. I'll catch up with
y'guys soon as I finish moppin'.

Hey assholes!
Now yer dealin' with me!

Matsunaga-aniki's got this.
Let's keep movin'.

Huh. Never figured there'd be
a tunnel under the shipyard.
Probly a mine shaft from before the war.

We've got a ways t'go.
Stay on me.

I brought some flashlights, jus' in case.
There's one fer each o' ya.
Try t'keep up, Aniki!
There's our exit!
Hey, did y'hear somethin'?

Someone's there!
Watch yourself!
D-Dammit...!
Wow, y'still standin'?

But don't go thinkin' that means
y'can take us down.
